reviewNotes:
LanSend 0.6.0 is a visual redesign of the iPhone app: a new app icon, an interface in the style of the system apps, and a tile layout on the Devices screen (tap a device tile to pick photos or files and send them in one step). Transfer behaviour, permissions, entitlements and the network protocol are unchanged from 0.5.1. No login, account, subscription, or internet service is required.

To test: put an iPhone and a Mac or Windows computer on the same Wi-Fi network. Open LanSend on both devices and allow Local Network access. Keep LanSend in the foreground on the iPhone. Send a small file to the iPhone, accept the incoming request, then find the received file in Files > On My iPhone > LanSend. To send from the iPhone, tap the computer's tile on the Devices screen and choose "Send photos and videos" or "Send files".

The com.apple.developer.networking.multicast entitlement is used to discover nearby peers through UDP multicast. The App ID has Apple's approved Multicast Networking capability, and the submitted app and provisioning profile include it. If a network blocks multicast, active subnet discovery is also used, and "Send to address" accepts a device's IP address directly. The network implementation is in Rust and uses HTTPS/TLS for transfers.

Local Network permission is used only for discovering and transferring files between devices on the same network. Photos selected by the user can be sent to another device. The app does not collect user data. Transfer confirmations, optional PIN protection, and paired-device certificate checks remain available.
